### Observed differences

- Activity A02 was present in about 46 in 100 traces in the earlier window (about 0.46 occurrences per trace, median normalized position about 0.11) and was not observed in any of the 200 later traces. [OCC002, POS002]
- Activity A01 shows the mirror image: not observed in the earlier window, it appears in about 50 in 100 later traces (about 0.5 occurrences per trace), also at an early position in the trace (median normalized position about 0.14). [OCC001, POS001]
- Earlier, A02 always occurred together with A03 in every trace where it appeared, in mixed order (A02 first in about 12 in 100 traces, A03 first in about 17, interleaved in about 18). In the later window, A01 likewise always occurs together with A03, usually after A03 or interleaved with it (A03 first in about 20 in 100 traces, interleaved in about 26, A01 first in about 5). [REL004, REL002]
- The successor sets match closely: earlier, A02 led mostly to A03 (about 32% of its outgoing transitions), A06 (about 22%), A11 (about 14%) and A13 (about 11%); later, A01 leads to A06 (about 24%), A03 (about 19%), A10 (about 15%), A11 (about 15%) and A13 (about 11%), plus smaller shares to A05, A04 and A09. A08, which A02 reached, is not among A01's observed successors. [DIR002, DIR001]
- A03's direct connections reflect the swap: earlier about 7% of A03's outgoing transitions went to A02; later that edge is unobserved and about 8% go to A01. [DIR003]
- The relationship with A06 carries over: earlier A02 co-occurred with A06 in about 26 in 100 traces; later A01 co-occurs with A06 in about 26 in 100 traces (A01 first in about 10, interleaved in about 13), while A06's own presence is stable (about 53 in 100 traces earlier, about 50 later). [REL005, REL003]
- A01 and A02 never occur in the same trace: earlier A02 appeared without A01 in about 46 in 100 traces; later A01 appears without A02 in about 50 in 100. [REL001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that A01 took over the role previously held by A02: A02, which appeared in roughly half of the earlier cases always alongside A03, is no longer observed, while A01 now appears in roughly half of the later cases, always together with A03, at a similarly early trace position, with a nearly identical successor set and the same co-occurrence pattern with A06. [OCC001, OCC002, REL001, REL002, REL004, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, REL003, REL005] The support is direct and consistent across occurrence, positional, directional and relational indicators, and the 12 qualifying items far exceed the roughly 0.21 expected by chance for the 43 tested units, so chance sampling cannot explain the pattern as a whole. [OCC001, OCC002, POS001, POS002, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005]

Limitations: zero participation only shows that A02 was not observed in the later window, and the evidence cannot establish that A01 and A02 are the same underlying step or that A01 occurs in exactly the cases where A02 used to; the replacement reading rests on the strong similarity of their profiles rather than on identity evidence. A competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is two independent changes — one activity dropped and a different one added — which would produce the same observations.

Other differences: beyond the A02-to-A01 edge swap, A03's remaining outgoing shares shifted slightly, with A10 rising from about 32% to about 37% of A03's outgoing transitions and A11 falling from about 24% to about 19%. [DIR003]
